brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Full bases piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,0,1, one stacked on the other.
A full-depth bin split into three compartments (bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-div3) sits on the top storey. One cell takes one bin, so 'bins' here means its three compartments, not separate bins.
drawer:0#0,1#cut is fitted on the cut face of the ground-floor half base piece:0,1,0, which is fixed to the stack with a double side connector.
capOpenFaces added solid end caps on all 10 open faces across both storeys, and check_build lists no open faces. lockJoints was also run.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey workbench organizer with 26 parts. Two full hex bases are stacked at cell 0,0. The top one holds a full-depth bin split into three compartments. A north-half base sits beside the ground floor at 0,1, joined to it with a double side connector, and a drawer fits its cut face. capOpenFaces put 10 solid end caps on every open face, and lockJoints ran afterwards. check_build shows no rule issues, and the collision check reads clear. I put a marker, a pen and a paint brush standing in the bin's three compartments to show what it's for.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
